title: The Road to Reims
description: June-July 1429. After the victory at Orleans, Joan of Arc must escort the Dauphin Charles through English-held territory to the cathedral at Reims for his coronation. English garrisons at Troyes and Chalons block the route and can be fought or persuaded to surrender. Victory requires the Dauphin reaching Reims cathedral alive; his death means defeat.

anachronisms_found: BERSERK as the 'raider chief' in Player Three's force: a Viking-culture unit some 400+ years out of period and out of region for 1429 Champagne; a Militia/Woad-free option such as a Militia, Brigand-style Knight, or even an Outlaw-flavoured Militia leader was available and would not have been anachronistic

The English garrison at Troyes/Chalons is built entirely from CROSSBOWMAN and PIKEMAN with no Longbowman, despite the Longbowman being the engine's signature and historically correct English unit for the Hundred Years' War

Player One's escorted VIP is a KING unit, i.e. an already-crowned monarch, when the entire premise is that Charles is the uncrowned Dauphin travelling to be crowned (defensible as an engine limit, but the flag/king iconography undercuts the narrative)
2,400 TREE_OAK on a 120x120 map turns the open chalk plains and vineyard country of Champagne between Troyes and Reims into dense forest

issues_found: Both active players are set to RANDOM civilization, so the architecture and unit skins for the French royal party and the English/Burgundian garrisons are undefined — the engine offers Franks and Britons, making this an avoidable error
The English garrison (Player 2) is built from CROSSBOWMAN and PIKEMAN with no LONGBOWMAN, the one unit the engine ships specifically to represent English forces of the Hundred Years' War
The 'raider chief' of the side quest is a BERSERK, a Viking unit of a wholly different culture and era; a Militia, Woad Raider-free generic unit or a renamed brigand would have served
No Burgundian presence at all, yet Troyes and Chalons were held by Anglo-Burgundian garrisons and the negotiations that opened them were with Burgundian-aligned townsmen

The brief promises garrisons that 'can be fought or persuaded to surrender', but the triggers encode only combat (Gate Breached on DESTROY_OBJECT); the historical surrenders of Troyes, Chalons and Reims without storm are absent
The scenario invents an English pikemen ambush and a peasant raider sub-plot ('slay their chief and our pikemen will march with you') that have no basis in the June-July 1429 march
GAIA roster of 2400 oak trees renders the open chalk plains of Champagne as dense forest
Only one town-scale settlement is built (a single CASTLE, GUARD_TOWER, MONASTERY and 18 wall segments); Troyes, Chalons and Reims are not distinguishable as separate places on the route

Both active players are set to civilization RANDOM, so the French escort and the English garrisons may render with Japanese, Aztec or Mongol architecture and unit skins — entirely avoidable, since Franks/Britons exist in the engine.

The English garrison at Troyes is armed with CROSSBOWMAN and PIKEMAN only; the defining English arm of the period, the Longbowman (available in the engine to a Briton player), is absent, and no English commander (Bedford, Talbot) is represented in any form.

Player 3's raider chief is a BERSERK — a Norse unit centuries and a culture removed from 1429 Champagne; a Militia-line or Woad-free generic unit, or a renamed Condottiero/Militia, would have been the correct stand-in for a French brigand captain.
The 'raiders plague our fields, slay their chief and our pikemen will join you' side quest is invented; nothing in the march to Reims corresponds to it.

No Reims cathedral is placed at the victory area — the only Monastery on the map belongs to Player 2 (the English garrison), so the coronation church the brief names as the goal has no physical representation.

The brief's key historical nuance — that Troyes and Chalons could be persuaded to surrender (Chalons opened its gates without a fight) — has no mechanic: only a 'Gate Breached' destroy trigger exists, so the towns can only be stormed.
Forces are token-sized (5 knights, 5 crossbowmen, 6 pikemen per garrison) rather than an army-scale royal progress.
